battle.name: 第二次鴉片戰爭
battle.brief: 一八五六年十月亞羅號事件掀開戰端，英法聯軍自珠江口打到京師。卡面線膛砲是遠征軍野戰砲兵的核心裝備，射程與穿甲力令清軍岸上固定砲台在交火前已被壓制；一八六〇年遠征軍奪取大沽口，九月二十一日在八里橋以砲火與騎兵側擊擊潰蒙古騎兵，十月五日進北京。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 交戰三方是英國、法國與清帝國。英方由倫敦的維多利亞政府主持，外交與用兵的授權出自樞密院與外交部，執行倚賴三套力量：一是駐紮香港與中國沿海的皇家海軍中國分隊，以數十艘蒸汽砲艇與巡洋艦執行封鎖與登陸；二是英國陸軍遠征部隊，步兵以英格蘭、蘇格蘭與愛爾蘭各營為骨幹，另有孟加拉軍、印度砲兵、廓爾喀與錫克部隊，1858年印度統治法頒布之前，印度部隊在編制上屬東印度公司軍，此後歸英王直轄；三是1858年奉命北上覲見的額爾金使團與隨行的海陸軍護衛。英方指揮分海陸兩線，海軍由分隊司令統一調度砲艇與登陸部隊，陸軍方面1857年至1860年由駐華部隊司令與海軍少將詹姆斯·霍普共同推動，1860年的遠征總指揮是全權特使額爾金，後勤則靠香港與印度接應。法國由拿破崙三世政府派出的遠征軍參戰，編制包括海軍步兵、法屬阿爾及利亞調來的祖安營與外籍兵團、安南與交趾支那的土兵，以及一支由蒸汽船與運兵船組成的分遣隊；海軍由熱努伊利中將率領，陸戰有巴爾訥准將，另有格羅男爵率領的外交使團，最終以使節在蓮花橋遇襲與清廷道歉為口實擴大干預。清方是咸豐帝治下的大帝國，軍隊分三層：京畿的八旗、察哈爾蒙古騎兵與健銳營、虎賁營、神機營由僧格林沁統一節制；地方是綠營與各省提督鎮標，兵力老舊、裝備散漫；新式勇營如湘軍、淮軍正在長江中下游與太平軍纏鬥，無力抽調北上。海上兵力是內洋水師與長江水師，多為沙船、縱帆船與廣船，靠火繩或燧發鳥槍配合少量前裝砲。
countriesEn: The three belligerents were Britain, France and the Qing Empire. On the British side the war was authorised in London by the Victorian government, with the Cabinet and the Foreign Office granting both the diplomatic and the military commissions, and it was carried out by three instruments. First, the Royal Navy's China Station, based on Hong Kong and the Chinese coast, with several dozen steam gunboats and cruisers to enforce the blockade and land the expeditionary force. Second, the British army expeditionary force, whose infantry was drawn from the English, Scottish and Irish regiments, supplemented by the Bengal Army, Indian artillery, Gurkha and Sikh troops; before the Indian Councils Act of 1858 the Indian units were formally part of the East India Company's armies and passed to the Crown afterwards. Third, the Elgin mission of 1858, sent north with a naval and military escort. British command was split between sea and shore: the commander-in-chief of the station coordinated the gunboats and the landings, the land effort between 1857 and 1860 was driven jointly by the commander of the forces in China and by Admiral James Hope, and the overall director of the 1860 expedition was the plenipotentiary Lord Elgin, with the commissariat fed from Hong Kong and India. France participated under Napoleon III through an expeditionary corps made up of marine infantry, zouaves and a Foreign Legion detachment drawn from Algeria, Annamite and Cochinchinese troops, and a detachment carried in steamships and transports. Admiral de Rigault de Genouilly led the navy and General Barne de Fouras the land forces, while Baron Gros headed the diplomatic mission; the killing of the envoys at the Lotus Bridge and the Chinese apologies afterwards gave France the pretext to widen its involvement. On the Qing side, the empire under the Xianfeng Emperor had three layers of forces. In the capital region the Eight Banners, the Chahar Mongol cavalry, the Jianrui and Hubu camps and the Divine Mechanism Division were all under Sengge Rinchen. At provincial level stood the Green Standard and the regional garrison troops, obsolete and poorly supplied. The new provincial armies, the Xiang and Huai formations, were locked in the Yangtze valley against the Taiping and could not be sent north. At sea the inner and Yangtze squadrons consisted largely of sand junks, junk-rigged vessels and broad-beamed ships armed with matchlock or flint gingals and a few muzzle-loading guns.
people: 英方最具影響力的是香港總督約翰·鮑靈，1856年10月的最後通牒由他發出，隨後英軍開戰；廣州英國專員巴夏禮自1858年起成為事實上的談判主角，他與譯員威妥瑪一同參與1860年通州的最後談判，與恭親王奕訢一方的談判最終破裂；海軍方面，西摩中將在1856年10月下令攻擊珠江口的虎門砲台，英國分隊司令詹姆斯·霍普少將主持了1857年與1860年兩次大沽口方向的作戰；1860年率軍入京並下令焚毀圓明園的是特使額爾金，其弟布里勒中校隨行在側，法國的遠征軍則由格羅男爵與巴爾訥准將分頭指揮海陸。戈登代表另一條戰線：他於1860年抵華，1862年接掌由華爾洋槍隊擴充而成的常勝軍，在太平軍戰場上嶄露頭角。法國使節格羅男爵在1860年6月18日蓮花橋一役被清軍射殺，法國公使布爾巴克同在隊中，此案直接引發後續的報復遠征。清方的關鍵人物是咸豐帝、主持對外談判的恭親王奕訢與軍機大臣肅順，掌北洋騎兵的僧格林沁是清廷倚重的將帥，八里橋敗後被奪去爵位；地方上，兩江總督何桂清在南京失守後逃往上游，馮子材在1858年鎮海與浙江一線抵禦法軍，主持鎮江防務的蒙古族水師提督海齡在城破後自盡。
peopleEn: The most influential Briton was the Hong Kong governor John Bowring, who issued the ultimatum of October 1856 before the war opened. The British commissioner at Canton, Harry Parkes, became the effective negotiator from 1858, travelling with the interpreter Thomas Wade into the final talks at Tongzhou in 1860, where discussions with Prince Gong and his colleagues finally broke down. On the naval side Admiral Seymour ordered the attack on the forts at the mouth of the Pearl River in October 1856, and the commander-in-chief of the China Station, Admiral James Hope, directed the Taku operations of 1857 and 1860. The man who led the army into Peking in 1860 and gave the order to burn the Old Summer Palace was the plenipotentiary Lord Elgin, his brother Colonel Buller beside him; in Paris the expedition was divided between the naval command of Baron Gros and General Barne de Fouras. Gordon represented another front: Charles Gordon reached China in 1860 and took over the Ever Victorious Army in 1862, built up from Ward's foreign-dragoon corps, and made his name against the Taiping. The French envoy Baron Gros was shot by Qing troops at the Lotus Bridge on 18 June 1860, with the French minister Alphonse de Bourbaki in the party, and the case directly triggered the punitive expedition of 1860. On the Chinese side the key figures were the Xianfeng Emperor, Prince Gong, who conducted the foreign negotiations, and the Grand Councillor Sukshen; Sengge Rinchen, commander of the northern cavalry, was the general on whom the court relied and was stripped of his title after the defeat at Baliqiao. In the provinces, the Liangjiang governor-general He Guiqing fled upstream after the fall of Nanking, Feng Zicai and the commanders of the Zhejiang line held the French at Zhenhai in 1858, and the Mongol admiral Hai Ling, who directed the defence of Zhenjiang, killed himself after the city fell.
kits: 卡面這門線膛口裝野戰砲是1850年代德國萊茵邦聯諸邦兵工廠的產品：膛線令彈丸在膛內旋轉、密封加強，同樣藥量可以走得更遠，精度亦優於滑膛砲；它由整箱備彈供應、以騾車牽引，砲手六至八人，通常配屬於一個步兵營或騎兵旅的砲兵連。英法遠征軍同期的同型武器是英國阿姆斯特朗1853年式的三十二磅線膛口裝砲，它在1857年12月的大沽口之戰第一次用於實戰，使英軍得以在清軍岸砲射程之外反擊；德國各邦製造的同類線膛野戰砲同期大量外銷，成為歐洲陸軍的標準配備。法軍的野戰砲隊同樣線膛化，並大量使用蒸汽砲艇與鐵殼汽船，其中尼米西斯號以鐵殼船身抵近清軍岸上砲位，是第一艘能以船身撞壞岸上固定砲的軍艦。清軍的對應火力是固定在城牆與砲台上的大口徑前裝砲，其中鎮江、燕子磯一帶的「無子大炮」重達數十噸，另有「花旗炮」等舊式重砲；步兵裝備則是抬槍、鳥槍、劈山槍與三眼銃這類火繩或燧發的前裝槍。清軍在南京與鎮江一線還曾把固定重砲架在城牆上對江射擊，射程雖遠，卻無法在線膛砲的射程內生存到第二輪齊射。英軍的攻城裝備則有火箭、相機測繪器材，以及用於觀察清軍縱隊的觀測氣球，氣球在1860年9月21日的八里橋之戰是首次用於戰爭。
kitsEn: The muzzle-loading rifled field gun on this card was a product of the arsenals of the German states of the Rhine Confederation in the 1850s. Rifling made the projectile rotate in the bore and tightened the seal, so that the same charge of powder carried further and with better accuracy than a smoothbore of the same calibre; the gun was served from boxed ammunition, towed by mule teams, worked by six to eight gunners, and normally attached to the battery of an infantry battalion or a cavalry brigade. The equivalent weapon in the Anglo-French expeditionary force was the British Armstrong 32-pounder rifled muzzle-loader of 1853, which first saw action at the Taku forts in December 1857 and allowed the British to reply from beyond the reach of the Qing shore batteries. Rifled muzzle-loading field guns of German manufacture were exported in large numbers at the same time and became standard equipment in European armies. The French field artillery was rifled as well and made heavy use of steam gunboats and iron steamers; among them the Nemesis brought her iron hull against the shore batteries and was the first warship able to smash a fixed shore gun with her own hull. The Qing reply was the heavy muzzle-loading gun mounted on city walls and in the forts, including the extraordinarily heavy childless cannon weighing several tens of tons at Zhenjiang and Yanziji, together with old-pattern heavy guns of the huachi type. Chinese infantry relied on pole guns, gingals, split-trail matchlocks and triple-barrelled fire-arms, matchlock or flint, and at Nanking and Zhenjiang the fixed heavy guns were mounted on the walls to fire down the river: their range was long, but they could not survive to a second salvo against a rifled gun firing from beyond their own reach. The British siege train added Congreve rockets, the camera and survey equipment of the Army Works Department, and an observation balloon used to watch the Chinese columns, the balloon being employed in war for the first time at the battle of Baliqiao on 21 September 1860.
tactics: 英法的戰術是海軍先制、陸軍跟進的兩段式。第一段是所謂「砲艦外交」：以分隊砲艇封鎖珠江口、長江口與白河海口，用封鎖切斷清廷的沿海貿易與漕運，再以登陸奪取砲台作為前進基地。1856年10月至12月的珠江口戰役，英軍以海軍陸戰隊攻取虎門兩岸的砲台，並沿江深入。1857年5月29日至31日攻取廣州，英軍由城北登陸，艦砲與野戰砲同時射擊城牆，步兵再以刺刀突入狹窄街巷與船艇密布的江面。1857年6月與9月，英國砲艇先後在九龍海面與廈門外海擊毀清軍水師船隊，使清廷喪失近海防衛的依賴。1858年英法聯軍沿長江內溯，砲艇隊推進至漢口，一度攻下鎮江與南京。1857年12月20日至26日與1858年9月21日兩度強攻大沽口：前者因灘塗淺水、潮汐不濟而未能登陸，並在夜間遭清軍火船襲擊；後者改以兩棲部隊在砲艇掩護下由灘頭強攻得手，白河航路自此打通。1860年的遠征軍再取大沽口，循海河、大清河與通州北上，9月21日在八里橋與清軍主力交鋒：蒙古騎兵以密集隊形反覆衝鋒，英軍以野戰砲連續射擊，並以印度騎兵自側翼衝擊，騎兵當場潰散，旗兵步卒亦告崩潰。遠征軍其後進軍北京，依托城牆與火砲的防禦在同樣的砲火面前迅速瓦解。全程補給靠海運與徵用當地船隻，北方鄉村的糧秣多被清軍徵發或焚毀，遠征軍曾因糧草不足而延誤行程。
tacticsEn: Anglo-French tactics had two stages: the navy first, the army following. The first stage was what came to be called gunboat diplomacy: a blockade of the mouth of the Pearl River, the mouth of the Yangtze and the mouth of the Peiho by the gunboats of the station, cutting the coastal trade and the grain tribute of the Qing, followed by landings that seized the forts and turned them into bases for the next move. In the Pearl River fighting of October to December 1856 British marines took the forts on both banks of the river and pushed upstream. The capture of Canton on 29 to 31 May 1857 was made from the north, with ship and field guns firing on the walls simultaneously, and the infantry then driving into narrow streets and a river crowded with boats. In June and September 1857 British gunboats destroyed the Qing fleet off the Kowloon coast and then off Amoy, and the court lost its reliance on coastal defence. In 1858 the Anglo-French force moved up the Yangtze, the gunboats reaching Hankou, and Nanking and Zhenjiang fell for a time. The two assaults on the Taku forts, from 20 to 26 December 1857 and on 21 September 1858, differed sharply. The first failed because of shallow mud flats and the tide, and the expedition was attacked at night by Chinese fire rafts. The second was a landing by amphibious troops on the flats under cover of the gunboats, and it opened the Peiho to shipping. The expedition of 1860 took the Taku forts again and marched inland by the Hai, the Taqing and Tongzhou. At Baliqiao on 21 September the Mongol cavalry charged again and again in dense formation; British field guns fired continuously and Indian cavalry struck the flank, and the charge broke at once, taking the Bannermen with it. The march into Peking followed, and the walls and fixed batteries facing it gave way under the same gunfire. Supply came by sea and by requisitioned local craft, and in the north the villages had their provisions taken or burned by the retreating Chinese, so that the expedition was delayed more than once for want of fodder and grain.
data: 時間跨度是1856年10月9日亞羅號事件到1860年10月24日《北京條約》簽訂，約四年。兵力方面：1857年5月攻取廣州的英軍約三千人、法軍不足千人；1857年12月第一次大沽口之戰，英法投入約三千至五千人（海軍陸戰隊與水兵為主）與數十艘砲艇，清軍守備據各方記錄約三千至五千人，四座砲台與城垣守軍約兩千，清方記錄陣亡約一千八百人，英方記錄則更低。1858年6月26日《天津條約》簽訂，同年9月21日第二次大沽口之戰，英法投入兵力以萬計、砲艇數十至九十餘艘，清守軍不足兩千，砲台在砲擊與突擊下失守。1860年的遠征軍，據英法雙方估計，英軍約八千人、法軍約七千人，合計約一萬五千人，野戰砲數十門。9月21日八里橋之戰，英法方面約三千五百人，含印度騎兵約六百人、野戰砲約四十門；清軍出動人數官方宣稱逾五萬，實際估計在兩萬至三萬之間，含綠營、旗兵、健銳營與蒙古騎兵，火砲約七十至八十門，清軍損失被記為逾千人，其餘潰散。裝備方面，尼米西斯號鐵殼汽船排水量約八百至一千噸，載有數門大口徑前裝砲；清軍「無子大炮」重達數十噸，並以固定基座安裝。賠款方面，兩份條約合計為數百萬兩白銀，法國另索二百萬法郎作為使節喪葬費。太平軍兵力在1860年前後被各方估為數十萬至百萬之數，使清廷無法集中全部兵力。
dataEn: The war ran from the Arrow incident of 9 October 1856 to the signing of the Convention of Peking on 24 October 1860, about four years. On numbers: the assault on Canton in May 1857 used about three thousand British and under a thousand French; at the first Taku action in December 1857 the Anglo-French force numbered roughly three to five thousand, mostly marines and sailors, supported by several dozen gunboats, against a Qing garrison recorded in different sources at between three and five thousand, of which about two thousand manned the four forts and the walls, and the Chinese records put their dead at about eighteen hundred, the British accounts lower. The Treaty of Tianjin was signed on 26 June 1858, and at the second Taku action on 21 September of that year the Anglo-French force numbered in the thousands up to ten thousand, with several dozen to more than ninety gunboats, against a garrison of fewer than two thousand, whose forts fell under gunfire and assault. The expedition of 1860 was estimated by both sides at about eight thousand British and seven thousand French, some fifteen thousand in all, with dozens of field guns. At Baliqiao on 21 September the Anglo-French side had roughly three thousand five hundred men, including about six hundred Indian cavalry and about forty field guns; the Chinese official figure was above fifty thousand, realistic estimates put the force actually engaged between twenty and thirty thousand, drawn from the Green Standard, the Banners, the Jianrui camp and the Mongol cavalry, with some seventy to eighty guns, the Chinese losses being recorded at over a thousand with the rest scattered. In equipment, the iron steamer Nemesis displaced roughly eight hundred to one thousand tons and carried several heavy muzzle-loading guns; the Chinese childless cannon weighed several tens of tons and were set on fixed platforms. In money, the two treaties provided for several million taels of silver in indemnity, with France claiming a further two million francs for the funerals of its envoys. The Taiping forces were estimated at several hundred thousand to a million men by 1860, which is why the Qing court could not concentrate everything on the north.
cause: 直接導火線是亞羅號事件。1856年10月9日，在廣州附近水域，一艘在香港註冊的英籍商船亞羅號被廣東水師的船員與官員登船查驗，一批華籍船員被帶走；英國領事要求放人，並要求廣州方面在期限內給出滿意答覆，期限過後仍無回應，香港總督鮑靈與英國海軍便決定以武力維護商船旗號與領事權威。此前一再被拒絕的要求，是英國使團循海路北上、到北京覲見皇帝並在北方設立常駐公使，這一要求直接觸及清廷的禮制與朝貢體系，被屢次擱置。深層原因是《南京條約》之後的通商體制仍舊限於廣州一港，並由十三行行商把持，洋商與地方官府的衝突長年累積；1840年代以來英國商人希望在華設永久代表處、擴大口岸與自由度，一直沒有進展。法國的介入起於1856年太平軍在廣西永安起事期間的傳教士遇害案件：法國傳教士在黔桂一帶被殺、教產被沒收，巴黎要求歸還教產並懲兇，兩國在1858年簽訂的條約中明確換取了法方的干預權。中國內部的局勢同樣是背景：太平軍自1850年代起席捲長江中下游，捻軍在淮北與中原此起彼伏，清廷在南北兩面受敵，禁不起大規模對外用兵，新式勇營正是在這個空檔裡成形，其影響也延續到1860年代以後。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was the Arrow incident. On 9 October 1856, in the waters near Canton, a British merchant ship registered in Hong Kong, the Arrow, was boarded and inspected by Guangdong naval officials and men, and a number of Chinese crew were taken away. The British consul demanded their release and a satisfactory answer within a fixed term; when the term expired without reply, Governor Bowling and the Royal Navy decided to use force to maintain the ship's flag and the authority of the consul. The standing demand that preceded it was for a British mission to travel by sea to Peking, to be received by the Emperor and to keep a permanent legation in the north, which struck at the ritual and the tributary system of the court and was deferred again and again. The deeper cause lay in the trading system after the Treaty of Nanking, still confined to the single port of Canton and brokered by the Cohong, with endless friction between foreign merchants and the local authorities; since the 1840s the British had wanted permanent representation in China, more ports and greater freedom, and had got nowhere. France came in over the case of the missionaries killed when the Taiping rose at Yong'an in Guangxi in 1856: French missionaries were killed in the Guizhou and Guangxi area and their church property was confiscated, and Paris demanded the return of the property and the punishment of the offenders, trading the agreement of 1858 for the right of intervention. Conditions inside China were a background of the same kind: the Taiping had swept the middle and lower Yangtze since the 1850s and the Nian rose and fell across the Huai and the plains, the court was pressed from north and south at once and could not afford a large war abroad, and the new provincial armies took shape precisely in that gap, an arrangement whose effects ran well past 1860.
impact: 這場戰爭把中國更深地嵌進列強的秩序，也把清廷的軍政弱點一次顯影。對英法而言，它確立了「砲艦外交」的範式：用封鎖代替常備陸軍，用條約代替割地，以通商口岸的制度性收益代替一時的領土佔領，此後數十年中國沿海的外交都以海軍為後盾。對中國而言，1858年《天津條約》與1860年《北京條約》帶來新開十處通商口岸（漢口、九江、鎮江、南京、福州、廈門、牛莊等）、外國使節常駐北京、內河航權與數百萬兩白銀賠款；九龍一地永久割予英國，廣州城被英軍佔領三年，外人在租界內取得近乎自治的權力，日後上海、天津、漢口的租界制度皆循此軌跡展開，列強在華的常駐兵力與巡邏權也自此固定。軍事上，線膛砲、鐵殼汽船與艦隊後膛砲證明了工業化火力對舊式城牆與固定砲台的壓倒性差距；清廷的應對是在江南製造總局、福州船政局等地設廠仿製，並以購買歐洲武器維持新式軍隊，此即洋務運動的物質起點。遠征軍在北方纏鬥的同時，太平軍仍在長江流域擴張；英法介入並未替清廷解除內患，反而把清軍主力牽制在北面，戰後清廷不得不借外債維持常勝軍等洋槍隊，內外之別反轉。國際層面上，同一批艦隊在1860年也出現在日本沿岸，幕府屈服後簽署通商條約並准許開港，日本的倒幕運動由此加速。
impactEn: The war pulled China deeper into the order of the great powers and laid bare the military and administrative weakness of the Qing at one stroke. For Britain and France it set the model of gunboat diplomacy: a blockade in place of a standing army, treaties in place of annexation, and the institutional returns of the treaty ports in place of any lasting territorial gain; Chinese diplomacy along the coast was backed by naval power for decades afterwards. For China the Treaty of Tianjin of 1858 and the Convention of Peking of 1860 brought ten additional treaty ports, among them Hankou, Kiukiang, Zhenjiang, Nanking, Foochow, Amoy and Niuchang, permanent legations in Peking, navigation on the inland waters and several million taels of silver in indemnity. Kowloon was ceded to Britain in perpetuity, Canton was held by British troops for three years, and foreigners in the concessions obtained something close to municipal autonomy; the concession system in Shanghai, Tianjin and Hankou followed the same track, and the foreign military presence and the right of patrol in China were thereafter fixed. Militarily the rifled gun, the iron steamer and the breech-loading naval gun demonstrated the decisive gap between industrial firepower and the old wall and the fixed battery. The Qing answer was to build arsenals at the Jiangnan Arsenal and the Fuzhou shipyard, to copy what they could and to buy European weapons so as to keep the new troops in being; that was the material starting point of the self-strengthening movement. While the expedition fought in the north the Taiping were still spreading along the Yangtze; Anglo-French involvement did not relieve the Qing of the internal enemy, it tied their main force to the north, and after the war the court had to fund the Ever Victorious Army and other foreign-dragoon corps with foreign loans, so that inside and outside exchanged places. At the international level the same squadrons appeared off Japan in 1860, the shogunate conceded, signed the commercial treaties and opened its ports, and the movement that would end the shogunate quickened in consequence.
result: 結果是清廷割地賠款、但並未在軍事上被摧毀。1858年6月26日《天津條約》簽訂，規定增開通商口岸、外國使節常駐北京、租用民宅與鴉片問題作最後處理；1860年10月24日《北京條約》作為補充，確認英法條約並把九龍割予英國，法國另取得二百萬法郎的使節喪葬費與教會權利條款。戰場上最關鍵的兩個結果都出現在北方：遠征軍在1860年9月21日的八里橋擊潰僧格林沁的京畿主力，10月5日進入北京，10月18日至21日圓明園的殿堂樓閣被縱火焚成焦土；海上則在四年內反覆證明同一件事——只要能控制砲艇與航路，清廷的沿岸防禦就形同虛設，廣州被攻陷後交由英軍佔管三年便是最直白的明證。戰役層面，四年戰事的勝負並非由某一場大會戰決定：廣州、鎮江、九龍海面、大沽口與八里橋的勝利，都由海軍封鎖與登陸配合完成，而清軍在每一處的崩潰都與其被牽制於太平軍戰線直接相關。戰爭本身沒有解決鴉片與通商體制的根本爭議，談判桌上的僵局反而促使英國在1860年代把目光投向更廣的亞洲航路與市場；而對清廷而言，這場戰爭留下的不只是賠款與割地，更是「靠買船買砲能不能追平列強」這個仍未有答案的問題。
resultEn: The result was a cession and an indemnity for the Qing, but no military destruction. The Treaty of Tianjin of 26 June 1858 provided for more treaty ports, permanent foreign legations in Peking, the leasing of houses and the final disposal of the opium question; the Convention of Peking of 24 October 1860 confirmed the Anglo-French treaties and ceded Kowloon to Britain, while France obtained two million francs for the funerals of its envoys and clauses on the rights of the missions. The two decisive results of the war lay in the north: the expedition broke Sengge Rinchen's capital field army at Baliqiao on 21 September 1860 and entered Peking on 5 October, and between 18 and 21 October the halls of the Old Summer Palace were put to the torch and left in ruins. At sea the same lesson was demonstrated again and again over four years: control of the gunboats and the channels made the Qing coastal defence a shell, and the three years in which Canton was administered by British troops is the plainest proof of it. On the field the outcome was not settled by any single great engagement: Canton, Zhenjiang, the fight off Kowloon, the two Taku actions and Baliqiao were all won by the combination of naval blockade and landing, and each Chinese collapse was tied directly to the fact that the army was tied down on the Taiping front. The war settled nothing fundamental about opium or the trading system, and the deadlock at the negotiating table only pushed Britain in the 1860s toward the wider Asian markets and sea routes. What the Qing were left with was not merely the indemnity and the cession, but the question of whether buying ships and guns could ever bring them level with the powers, and that question was still unanswered.
